brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Keyhole hangers accessory:0#0,-1#2 and accessory:0#2,-2#2 sit on the wall-facing side (slot 2) of the two back cells. Those faces lie in one plane, so both rest flat against the wall. The configurator checks fit only: it doesn't check how much weight the plastic hangers or the wall screws can hold.
bin:0,-1,0, bin:1,-1,0 and bin:2,-2,0 (hex-bin-full-div2): 3 bins with 2 compartments each.
2 hex-acc-keyhole hangers; capOpenFaces left those faces uncapped. The middle cell has no hanger of its own: it hangs from the back cells by joint bolts jointBolt:0#0,-1#0 and jointBolt:0#1,-1#1.

finish.summary: I built a wall-hung spice rack from three full hex bases in a zig-zag row: (0,-1), (1,-1) and (2,-2). Each base holds a full-depth bin split into 2 compartments, so there are 3 bins and 6 spice compartments. The two back cells each carry a keyhole hanger on the face toward the wall. Those two faces line up in one flat plane, so the rack drops onto two screws already in the wall. The middle cell sits half a cell forward and is held by joint bolts. The house rules are done: 12 solid end caps on the other open faces and 2 joint bolts, 20 parts in all. check_build reports no issues and the mesh check is clear. The props catalog has no spice jars, so I didn't add any props, and I didn't confirm the layout by eye: the one camera view I took listed no props and no image, since there were none to show.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
